description: Labelled triage set for the Jev vs Pi-model comparison. Requests are short, realistic asks a user might give a coding agent in this repository. Labels were assigned by the author following the policy text below, which is also the text every arm receives; there is no external gold set.

policy.type: Classify the request with exactly one type: bug (restore broken intended behavior, including regressions), feature (add or intentionally change capability), refactor (restructure without changing observable behavior), docs (documentation, agent instructions or policy text only), test (verification only, no product behavior change), chore (dependencies, configuration, builds, routine maintenance), research (a tracked investigation or measurement artifact; a read-only question counts here).
policy.effort: Choose one ordered level for how much of the repository the request needs: 0 = one file at a known seam; 1 = a few files inside one module; 2 = cross-module or multi-repository work; 3 = architecture-level change.
policy.approval: Answer yes only when the request itself is a reserved user-owned decision that the agent must not act on before the user approves: pushing or promoting to main, deleting files or data, changing credentials or permissions, or installing or removing software. Otherwise answer no.
